chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Ali al-Jarmi, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah and Durust, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a person in ihram who threw [a stone] at game and hit its leg, causing it to limp. He said: 'If the gazelle walked on it and grazed while he was looking at it, there is no penalty upon him. But if the gazelle went off on its own while he was raising it [to check], he does not know what it did, so the ransom is upon him because he does not know, perhaps it has perished.'

key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: A pilgrim in the state of ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the fidya (ransom) for accidentally killing game while in ihram?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a nuanced legal principle distinguishing between clear survival and uncertain death, requiring the fidya (ransom) only when the pilgrim is unsure if the game perished, thereby emphasizing the role of doubt (shakk) in determining liability. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential focus on the pilgrim's state of knowledge regarding the animal's fate at the moment of the strike. It serves as a foundational text for understanding how uncertainty in the outcome of an action influences the obligation of expiation in Hajj rituals.
